artifacts.summary: 6-phase plan in 5 dependency waves (8.5h) for the Stop-branch completion announcement, the idle_prompt matcher widening, the pane-keyed cooldown, and the two documentation reconciliations.

memory_candidates.content: When a hook/trigger matcher STRING is widened in a system whose deploy merge engine is additive-only (it adds a fragment's blocks but never retracts a changed or removed one), the already-deployed tree ends up carrying BOTH the old and the new matcher block. An event matching both then fires the same handler twice. The planning consequence is a hard phase-ordering constraint that is invisible if you reason only about the source store: any dedup, cooldown, or idempotence guard must land in an EARLIER phase than the matcher widening, otherwise the widening itself manufactures the duplicate-fire burst the guard exists to prevent. Generalizes to any additive-only config merge (permission grants, server registrations, hook blocks), not just TTS matchers.
